This approach aims to preserve crucial task-related information while introducing diversity in the training data. The DDA method applies a random augmentation from a set of possible augmentations to the background pixels, while D3A uses a Q-value distance metric to determine whether to apply the augmentation, aiming for semantic invariance. The authors evaluate these methods on the DeepMind Control Suite (DMC-GB) benchmark, specifically focusing on generalization scenarios involving color changes and background videos. The paper argues that by focusing on the primary pixels and diversifying the background, their methods achieve better sample efficiency and generalization to unseen environments. The authors present a detailed methodology, including the architecture of the encoder-decoder model and the process of segmenting primary pixels using k-means clustering. The paper also introduces the concept of semantic-invariant state transformation, which is assessed using the Q-value distance. Overall, the paper presents a novel approach to data augmentation in visual RL, with promising empirical results on the DMC-GB benchmark.
